buildings.name: Pons Sublicius (regal)
buildings.summary: The oldest bridge of Rome, built entirely of wood on piles (sublicae) and fastened without iron, the bridge Horatius Cocles held against Porsenna. It crossed the Tiber from the Forum Boarium near the Porta Trigemina just below the later Pons Aemilius; its exact position is debated (Coarelli just downstream of the Pons Aemilius; others nearer the Aventine).

phases.t: Built by Ancus Marcius according to tradition, of timber held together without iron so that it could be dismantled.

scholarship: Taylor, 'Tiber river bridges and the development of the ancient city of Rome', The Waters of Rome 2 (2002)
buildings.note: Placed about 170 m below the Pons Aemilius, between the Porta Trigemina and the Salinae, crossing roughly perpendicular to the southward current. Length assumes an ancient river about 110 m wide here. Number of pile bents unknown (10 assumed).

buildings.name: Pons Sublicius (Republican)
buildings.summary: The oldest bridge of Rome, built entirely of wood on piles (sublicae) and fastened without iron, the bridge Horatius Cocles held against Porsenna. It crossed the Tiber from the Forum Boarium near the Porta Trigemina just below the later Pons Aemilius; its exact position is debated (Coarelli just downstream of the Pons Aemilius; others nearer the Aventine).

phases.t: Cut down behind Horatius Cocles against Porsenna (508); repeatedly carried away by floods and rebuilt in timber under the care of the pontifices.

scholarship: Taylor, 'Tiber river bridges and the development of the ancient city of Rome', The Waters of Rome 2 (2002)
buildings.note: Placed about 170 m below the Pons Aemilius, between the Porta Trigemina and the Salinae, crossing roughly perpendicular to the southward current. Length assumes an ancient river about 110 m wide here. Number of pile bents unknown (10 assumed).

buildings.name: Pons Sublicius (Imperial)
buildings.summary: The oldest bridge of Rome, built entirely of wood on piles (sublicae) and fastened without iron, the bridge Horatius Cocles held against Porsenna. It crossed the Tiber from the Forum Boarium near the Porta Trigemina just below the later Pons Aemilius; its exact position is debated (Coarelli just downstream of the Pons Aemilius; others nearer the Aventine).

phases.t: Swept away in the flood of 23 BC (Cassius Dio 53.33.5) and rebuilt; restored again by Antoninus Pius; still listed among the bridges in the 4th-century Notitia. Possibly given stone piers in the Empire, timber deck kept for religious reasons.

scholarship: Taylor, 'Tiber river bridges and the development of the ancient city of Rome', The Waters of Rome 2 (2002)
buildings.note: Placed about 170 m below the Pons Aemilius, between the Porta Trigemina and the Salinae, crossing roughly perpendicular to the southward current. Length assumes an ancient river about 110 m wide here. Number of pile bents unknown (10 assumed).

buildings.name: Pons Aemilius (piers of 179 BC, timber deck)
buildings.builderName: the censors M. Aemilius Lepidus and M. Fulvius Nobilior
buildings.summary: The first stone bridge of Rome: in 179 BC the censors laid stone piers (pilae) across the Tiber from the Forum Boarium to Transtiberim, carrying a wooden deck.
buildings.note: Axis from the surviving arch of the Ponte Rotto: the remnant pier block (OSM) has its short sides along about 77/257 degrees, the bridge running from the bridgehead by the Casa dei Crescenzi (left bank) obliquely WSW to Transtiberim; endpoints set at the modern embankments.

buildings.name: Pons Aemilius (stone arches)
buildings.builderName: the censors P. Cornelius Scipio Aemilianus and L. Mummius
buildings.summary: In 142 BC the censors vaulted the piers of 179 BC with arches, making the Pons Aemilius the first fully stone bridge over the Tiber.
buildings.note: Six arches assumed (as in the medieval bridge); spans about 24 m at the centre.

buildings.name: Pons Aemilius (Augustan rebuilding)
buildings.summary: Rebuilt by Augustus (an inscription of 12 BC is attributed to it) with travertine facing and flood openings over the piers; repaired often (Probus, 280; late antiquity). It stood through our period; its last arch survives as the Ponte Rotto after the flood of 1598.
scholarship: Taylor, 'Tiber river bridges', The Waters of Rome 2 (2002)
buildings.note: Ruin of one arch in mid-river at the given axis point (OSM Ponte Rotto, 41.88934 N 12.47937 E).

buildings.name: Pons Fabricius
buildings.summary: The oldest Roman bridge still in use: built in 62 BC by L. Fabricius, curator viarum, from the Campus Martius (by the Theatre of Marcellus) to the Tiber Island, with two arches of about 24.5 m and a small flood arch over the central pier. Restored in 21 BC by the consuls M. Lollius and Q. Lepidus (inscriptions on both faces).

phases.t: Built by L. Fabricius (CIL VI 1305), replacing a wooden bridge of 192 BC.
Inspected and approved by the consuls M. Lollius and Q. Aemilius Lepidus after the flood of 23 BC.

buildings.note: Line from the OSM deck way (Ponte Fabricio), left bank NE to the island SW; length 62-65 m, width 5.5 m. Deck elevation estimated (about 14 m above mean water).

buildings.name: Pons Cestius
buildings.builderName: a Cestius (perhaps L. Cestius, praetor 44 BC)
buildings.summary: Bridge from the Tiber Island to Transtiberim, of uncertain late-Republican date (c. 46 BC), with one main arch of 23.65 m flanked by small flood arches.
buildings.note: Island end from the OSM deck; the Transtiberim end placed 52 m along the axis (the ancient bridge was about 48.5 m long; the 1888-92 rebuilding lengthened it to 80 m when the channel was widened).

buildings.name: Pons Gratiani (Pons Cestius rebuilt)
buildings.summary: Rebuilt in 365-370 by the emperors Valentinian, Valens and Gratian, partly with travertine from the Theatre of Marcellus, and dedicated as the Pons Gratiani (inscriptions CIL VI 1175-1176).

phases.t: Dedicated as Pons Gratiani under Valentinian, Valens and Gratian.

buildings.name: Pons Agrippae
buildings.summary: Bridge named after Agrippa, known from a cippus of the curatores riparum of AD 147 and from piers found in the riverbed in 1887 about 120 m upstream of the Ponte Sisto; it linked the Campus Martius by the Euripus/Stagnum district with Transtiberim. It may have been replaced by the Pons Aurelius on the Ponte Sisto site.

phases.t: Repaired under Antoninus Pius (cippus CIL VI 31545).

scholarship: Taylor, 'Tiber river bridges', The Waters of Rome 2 (2002)
buildings.note: Position from the 1887 riverbed finds (about 120 m upstream of Ponte Sisto), axis parallel to Ponte Sisto. Some scholars identify it with the Pons Aurelius/Antoninus. Date of construction (Agrippa's works of c. 25 BC) and end date (not in the 4th-century list, so perhaps ruined or superseded; shown as foundations from 400) are uncertain.

buildings.name: Pons Aurelius (Pons Antoninus)
buildings.summary: The bridge on the site of the Ponte Sisto, named Aurelius (Notitia) and probably built or rebuilt by an Antonine emperor (Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, i.e. Caracalla, is often preferred), carrying the Via Aurelia's city route from the Campus Martius into Transtiberim. From 271-275 it was joined to the Aurelian Wall at the Porta Aurelia/Septimiana side.
buildings.note: Line from the OSM deck of Ponte Sisto (whose piers stand on the ancient foundations). Date of construction uncertain (Antonine; 212-215 assumed).

buildings.name: Pons Valentiniani (Pons Aurelius rebuilt)
buildings.builderName: Valentinian I and Valens; the urban prefect L. Aurelius Avianius Symmachus

arch.note: arch of Valentinian and Valens at the Campus Martius end

buildings.summary: Rebuilt in 365-367 by Valentinian and Valens and dedicated by the prefect Symmachus with a triumphal arch at its left-bank end, whose bronze statues and inscriptions were recovered from the river in 1878-92. Below it in 537 Belisarius moored his floating mills. Damaged in 792, it was rebuilt as the Ponte Sisto in 1473-79.

phases.t: Belisarius' floating mills moored in the current below the bridge (Procopius 5.19.19-22).

buildings.name: Pons Neronianus (Pons Triumphalis)
buildings.summary: Imperial bridge from the Campus Martius (end of the later Via Recta) to the Vatican plain, the Horti Agrippinae and the Circus of Gaius and Nero, built by Caligula or Nero. Missing from the 4th-century bridge list, it was probably ruined or deliberately broken by then; low-water remains of its piers lie just below the Ponte Vittorio Emanuele II near S. Spirito.
buildings.note: Axis and position estimated from the low-water pier remains about 40 m downstream of Ponte Vittorio Emanuele II (OSM deck 12.4648 41.9008 to 12.4639 41.9015). Construction date (40-50) and ruin date (by 400) approximate.

buildings.name: Pons Aelius
buildings.summary: Hadrian's bridge to his mausoleum, dedicated in 134: three main arches of 18.4 m over the river and sloping ramps on small arches at each end (three on the Campus side, two on the mausoleum side), faced in travertine. From 271-275 the mausoleum became a bridgehead fortress of the Aurelian Wall. The three central arches survive in the Ponte Sant'Angelo.

phases.t: Integrated into the defences of the Mausoleum/Castellum under Honorius.

buildings.note: Axis from the OSM deck of Ponte Sant'Angelo; total length with ramps about 135 m (the modern bridge's outer arches replaced the ramps in 1892-94).

buildings.name: Pons Probi
buildings.summary: Bridge built under Probus (276-282) below the Aventine, linking the Emporium and Marmorata with Transtiberim near the Porta Portuensis.
buildings.note: Remains seen near the Marmorata (Via Marmorata / Arco di S. Lazzaro) and removed in 1484; crossing placed opposite them, about 180 m downstream of the modern Ponte Sublicio.

buildings.name: Pons Theodosii (Pons Probi restored)
buildings.summary: Restored under Theodosius (381-387) and thereafter called Pons Theodosii; Symmachus' letters complain of the slow work. It fell in the 11th century.

notes: Pons Milvius lies at about 41.9356 N 12.4671 E, just outside the model area (north edge 41.935), so it is not included. Line runs bank to bank; 'deckElev' is the estimated roadway level in m asl (mean Tiber about 6.5 m asl); 'h' is deck-crown height above mean water. Arch counts: 'arches' = all arches including ramp and flood arches where known.
